newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: SOCCER-MEXICO WIN CONTROVERSIAL GAME IN EL SALVADOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO WIN CONTROVERSIAL GAME IN EL SALVADOR.

text.p: Mexico beat El Salvador in controversial style on Sunday, scoring the only goal from what their opponents thought was an offside position and then surviving a last-minute penalty appeal.

El Salvador players protested that Mexican striker Luis Garcia, who came on as a halftime substitute, was offside when he scored in the 66th minute after finding himself all alone with only goalkeeper Raul Garcia to beat.
One minute from time, El Salvador players claimed they should have had a penalty when Elias Montes went flying in the Mexican penalty area. But Argentine referee Hugo Cordero ignored their appeals.
Angry fans in the 40,000 crowd hurled objects onto the pitch and the game was held up for four minutes.
The win left Mexico as comfortable leaders of the six-team group final round group and almost certain to qualify for France next year.
Mexico have 11 points, four more than second-place Costa Rica.

The United States, Canada and Jamaica each have five and El Salvador are last on four. Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica have played five games and the other teams four. The top three qualify for France.

El Salvador - Raul Garcia, Wilfredo Iraheta, Vladan Vicevic, Roberto Martinez, Jorge Rodriguez, Alexander Amaya (Sergio Valencia), Ronald Cerritos, Luis Lazo (Waldir Guerra), Mauricio Cienfuegos, Raul Diaz Arce (William Renderos), Elias Montes.

Mexico - Adolfo Rios, Pavel Pardo, Claudio Suarez, German Villa, Duilio Davino, Marcelino Bernal, Ramon Ramirez, (Cuahtemoc Blanco), Alberto Coyote (Luis Garcia), Alberto Garcia Aspe, Camilo Romero, Carlos Hermosillo.
